Best alternative to token-optimizer-mcp

Tokenade

Output Filtering

Format-aware compactors cover git, cargo, kubectl, terraform, docker and more — 60–99% reduction on the noisiest commands. Command rewriting further trims source-side before the shell even runs.

token-optimizer-mcp

Output Filtering

Smart replacements for Read, Grep and Glob with claimed 80–90% reduction; persistent Brotli-compressed SQLite cache avoids re-fetching identical outputs across sessions.

Tokenade

Semantic Code Search

Finds the most relevant files for a task and sends only those to the model, instead of the whole repo. Runs fully on-device with no external vector database and no model downloads — fast even on large codebases.

token-optimizer-mcp

Semantic Code Search

Not available as a dedicated feature. token-optimizer-mcp compresses file reads but does not build a semantic or structural index of the codebase.

Tokenade

Skeleton Compression

Signatures-only view of source files, YAML, Markdown and Terraform — −64% on file reads while preserving every top-level declaration. Stacks on top of output filtering for maximum savings.

token-optimizer-mcp

Multi-tier Caching & Compression

Multi-tier LRU/LFU/FIFO cache backed by SQLite + Brotli. In-memory session cache reduces compression overhead from 50–70 ms to <10 ms. tiktoken counts guard against over-sized responses.

Tokenade

Third-Party MCP Optimization

tokenade mcp-proxy wraps any third-party MCP server's launch command in the agent's MCP config, so every tool result (verbose JSON, logs, console output) is folded on the way back — set once, not per call. Image results pass through untouched.

token-optimizer-mcp

MCP Tool Catalog

61+ specialized MCP tools with session caching (first call scans, rest instant). No lazy-loading by default — the full manifest is exposed unless manually pruned.

Tokenade

Mechanism Breadth

The only tool combining output filtering + semantic search + skeleton compression + sandbox execution + MCP proxying + secret redaction + content-addressed cache in a single binary. On the open THOL benchmark it is the only one of the twelve tools tested that measurably cuts costs: 23% cheaper than running no tool at all, and 39% cheaper on long sessions.

Mechanism Breadth

Output filtering + multi-tier caching + 7-phase global hooks + session analytics in one MCP server. No codebase indexing or semantic search.

Tokenade

Savings Dashboard

tokenade dashboard shows measured savings, per-command and per-project breakdown, and framework-detection status. Local logs rotate automatically with built-in secret redaction.

token-optimizer-mcp

Session Analytics

Per-hook, per-action and per-MCP-server token savings breakdown within the session. Granular cost attribution is the strongest analytics offering among MCP-only tools.

token-optimizer-mcp at a glance

token-optimizer-mcp starts at Free. TypeScript MCP server with 61+ specialized tools, multi-tier LRU/LFU/FIFO caching backed by SQLite + Brotli, global 7-phase hooks and session analytics, claiming 60–90% reduction across 38,000+ real-world operations.

Pros

  • Massive tool inventory covering edge cases: Docker, network diagnostics, processes, DB optimization
  • Persistent SQLite cache survives sessions and uses Brotli compression (50–70 ms → <10 ms after warm-up)
  • 7-phase hook system automates optimization on every tool call automatically
  • Per-hook/per-action/per-MCP-server granular analytics breakdown
  • Handles both file-read compression and output filtering in one MCP server

Cons

  • No codebase indexing or semantic/dependency graph — purely compression-based
  • Hooks are installed globally via a postinstall npm script, which can conflict with other tools
  • 61+ tools adds significant MCP manifest overhead unless lazy-loading is applied
  • Node.js runtime required; heavier startup than a compiled Rust/Go binary
